summary: Pratapaditya Pal is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and Cambridge. He served as a curator at the MFA Boston, LACMA, and the Art Institute of Chicago.

Prayag Raj Sharma works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at Tribhuvan University, including as Dean of the Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies (attested 1973) and as Professor (attested 1976–1990).
Prayoon Mererk is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi in 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark was a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics (~1935–1939), and served in the Office of Strategic Services (~1943–1945).

Priyanku Chakraborty specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Aishwarya Biswas, he served as Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellow in Buddhist Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Priyavrat Sharma was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. His career included serving as Director at Banaras Hindu University, including its Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Oslo, the Sorbonne, and Mainz, he held professorships at the University of Mainz (1980–1985) and Harvard University (~1991–2015).
Przemysław Szczurek is an Indologist who held posts at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań and at the University of Breslau, where he served as Professor of Indology (~2004).
Pulinbihari Chakravarti studied Indology and philosophy under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society (attested 1951).
Punyavijaya was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He founded the Prakrit Text Society.

Purna Harsha Bajracharya worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 1972, he was attested as Chief Research Officer at both the Archaeological Survey of India and the Department of Archaeology.

Purnima Dhavan is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Virginia. She held appointments at Bowdoin College, St. John's University, and the University of Washington (2005).
Purushottam Mahadev Joshi was an Indologist and historian. He worked at the University of Mumbai Library (~1935–1947) and later served as Reader in Medieval History at Deccan College (~1965–1970).

Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at the University of Mumbai and Harvard, he held academic posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi (1957–1960).

Purushottama Bilimoria is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Shivesh Thakur and earned a PhD at La Trobe University, later holding posts at Deakin University and the University of Melbourne.

Pushpendra Kumar, an Indologist who studied under Satya Vrat Shastri, served as a Sanskrit lecturer at the University of Delhi (~1965–2001) and as Principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.
Puthezhethu Rama Menon was active in Indology. He served as a judge on the Chief Court of Cochin and as President of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at King's College London by 2014 and served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

Péter-Dániel Szántó is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at Oxford, All Souls College, and Eötvös Loránd University.
Qian Cao is an Indology and philosophy scholar at Ghent University, where she is attested in 2026 as both a PhD student and faculty member.
